name: valet
description: Menswear outfits from the clothes you own, dressed for the weather and the occasion.

interface.longDescription:
Valet is a menswear stylist. Tell it what's in your wardrobe and where you're going, and it builds complete outfits: colour harmony, formality matched to the occasion, and the right layers for the day's forecast. Ask "what should I wear in Berlin tomorrow?" and it reads the weather and tells you whether you need a coat, what rain rules out, and which of your pieces to put on. Ask "does olive go with burgundy?" and you get a straight answer with the reason.

It's the engine behind the Valet iPhone app, which does the same from photos of your actual wardrobe. Menswear only for now. No account needed, and nothing you send is stored.
capabilities: Builds complete outfits from the clothes you describe
Dresses you for a city's forecast: coat, layers, rain
Says whether colours work together, and why
defaultPrompt: What should I wear in London tomorrow?
Build a work outfit from: navy blazer, white shirt, grey trousers, brown loafers

positive.description: Builds outfits for work from a described wardrobe.
positive.prompt: My clothes: navy wool overcoat, grey crewneck sweater, white oxford shirt, dark indigo jeans, stone chinos, brown suede chelsea boots, white leather sneakers. What should I wear to work?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls build_outfit with occasion work and the listed pieces; returns up to three complete looks (top, trousers, shoes, optional layer) with the reasoning for each, and a Valet look card.

positive.description: Styles a specific new piece across every look.
positive.prompt: I just bought stone chinos. How do I style them with: white oxford shirt, navy blazer, brown loafers, grey sweater, white sneakers?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls build_outfit with must_include ["stone chinos"]; every returned look contains the stone chinos.

positive.description: Dresses for tomorrow's forecast in a named city.
positive.prompt: What should I wear in London tomorrow?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls dress_for_weather with London's coordinates and timezone Europe/London; the answer states the forecast (temperature, rain) and whether a coat and how many layers are needed.

positive.description: Judges whether two colours work together.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls check_colors with navy and brown; the verdict is that they work, both reading as neutrals, with the reason.

positive.description: Combines the forecast with the person's own pieces for an occasion.
positive.prompt: It's a date tonight in New York. I have black jeans, white tee, olive field jacket, cream knit, brown chelsea boots. What should I wear?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls dress_for_weather with New York's coordinates, timezone America/New_York, the listed pieces and occasion date; returns the evening forecast and a complete look from those pieces suited to it.

negative.description: Unrelated creative request; no Valet tool should run.
negative.prompt: Write me a poem about autumn.

negative.description: Too few pieces for a complete outfit; build_outfit should explain what is missing rather than invent garments.
negative.prompt: Build an outfit from: navy overcoat, white shirt.

negative.description: Unknown colour name; check_colors should name the unrecognised colour back instead of guessing.

publication.release_notes: First release: build_outfit, dress_for_weather and check_colors. Read-only, no sign-in, nothing stored.
